title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Knowledge of Biotechnology - Biotechnology - Genetics, microbiology, sterilization landmarks
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Prior to the late 19th century, many believed that microbes simply appeared out of thin air via "spontaneous generation." Which historical experiment definitively debunked this theory and proved that airborne contamination causes microbial growth, establishing the foundation for modern aseptic technique and sterilization?
options: Gregor Mendel's mathematical modeling of trait inheritance in garden peas.
Louis Pasteur's famous swan-neck flask experiments with sterilized broth.
James Watson and Francis Crick's publication on the double-helix geometry of DNA.
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's initial discovery of bacteria using a rudimentary microscope.
questions.explain:
In 1859, **Louis Pasteur** utilized swan-neck (S-shaped) glass flasks filled with sterilized broth to trap airborne dust and microbes in the bend of the neck, keeping the broth sterile indefinitely despite being exposed to air. 

This elegant experiment definitively disproved spontaneous generation and formed the fundamental basis for the "Germ Theory of Disease" and modern lab sterilization protocols (like pasteurization and autoclaving).

questions.q: For decades, scientists debated whether complex proteins or simple DNA carried genetic information. The definitive experiment settling this debate utilized bacteriophages radioactively labeled with Phosphorus-32 (to track DNA) and Sulfur-35 (to track protein) to see which molecule entered the bacterial host cell. This landmark 1952 study is known as the:
questions.explain:
The **Hershey-Chase blender experiment** provided the final, undeniable proof that DNA is the genetic material. 

By labeling viral DNA with radioactive Phosphorus ($^{32}P$) and the viral protein coat with radioactive Sulfur ($^{35}S$), they infected bacteria and spun them in a centrifuge. They found only the $^{32}P$ (DNA) inside the bacterial cells, proving the virus injected DNA—not protein—to program the bacteria to build more viruses. 
> *Meselson-Stahl* (Option 'c') proved semi-conservative replication. 
> *Griffith/Avery* (Options 'b', 'd') showed DNA was the "transforming principle" earlier, but lacked the finality of Hershey-Chase.

questions.q: In 1982, the FDA issued its very first approval for a commercially available recombinant DNA pharmaceutical. This vital biologic drug was synthesized in engineered *E. coli*, replacing the historical need to extract the protein from the pancreases of slaughtered pigs and cattle. What was this landmark product?
questions.explain:
In 1982, Genentech and Eli Lilly achieved FDA approval for **Humulin (recombinant human insulin)**. 

Prior to this, diabetics relied on insulin extracted from pig and cow pancreases, which was inefficient and caused allergic reactions in some patients. Synthesizing the exact human insulin sequence in *E. coli* proved that genetically engineered bacteria could serve as pharmaceutical "factories," permanently changing the landscape of drug manufacturing.
